title: Proper-support direct image of a finite-Tor complex has finite Tor dimension
statement: Let S be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], let f:X\to S be a morphism locally of finite type, and let E be an object of D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. Assume E is bounded with coherent cohomology sheaves, every cohomology sheaf of E has support proper over S [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base], and E has finite Tor dimension as an object of D(f^{-1}\mathcal O_S). Then Rf_*E [def-pc-derived-direct-image] has finite Tor dimension as an object of D(\mathcal O_S): there are integers a\le b such that H^i(Rf_*E\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal F)=0 for every i\notin[a,b] and every \mathcal O_S-module \mathcal F.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.27.1 (Tag 08EV; label lemma-perfect-direct-image), proof, from 'Hence it suffices to show that Rf_*E has finite tor dimension' to the end (uses Tags 08EA, 08EU base change, Cohomology 08DZ variant derived pullback)

proof.text: By [lem-pc-direct-image-qc-support-reduction] (S Noetherian, f locally of finite type, E bounded with coherent cohomology whose cohomology sheaves have support proper over S) there is a quasi-compact open immersion j:X'\to X containing all supports of the H^i(E) with f'=f\circ j quasi-compact and quasi-separated and Rf'_*j^*E\cong Rf_*E. The hypotheses on E pass to j^*E (restriction to an open is exact and j^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal O_S=f'^{-1}\mathcal O_S, so the finite Tor interval [a,b] of E over f^{-1}\mathcal O_S is one for j^*E). Replace X,f,E by X',f',j^*E. Since S is Noetherian, hence quasi-compact, [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-uniform-truncation-bound] applies to f and gives an integer N.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.27.1 (Tag 08EV), reduction to a quasi-compact morphism using proper supports

proof.text: Let F be a quasi-coherent O_S-module. By [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] (with N=0) choose a complex P of flat O_S-modules with P^i=0 for i>0 and a quasi-isomorphism P\to F. By [lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback] Lf^*F is represented by the termwise pullback f^*P, which is K-flat over O_X by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat] and [lem-pc-kflat-pullback-preservation]; so E\otimes^L_{O_X}Lf^*F is computed termwise by E\otimes_{O_X}(O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}O_S}f^{-1}P)=E\otimes_{f^{-1}O_S}f^{-1}P (associativity of the tensor product). The terms f^{-1}P^i are flat f^{-1}O_S-modules (stalks (f^{-1}P^i)_x=P^i_{f(x)} over (f^{-1}O_S)_x=O_{S,f(x)}), so f^{-1}P is K-flat over f^{-1}O_S by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat] applied on the ringed space (X,f^{-1}O_S), and f^{-1}P\to f^{-1}F is a quasi-isomorphism since f^{-1} is exact. Hence E\otimes^L_{O_X}Lf^*F\cong E\otimes^L_{f^{-1}O_S}f^{-1}F, which by the finite Tor-dimension hypothesis has cohomology only in [a,b], with a\le b independent of F.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.27.1 (Tag 08EV), the identity Lf^*F tensor E = f^{-1}F tensor_{f^{-1}O_S} E (Cohomology, variant derived pullback)

proof.text: E has coherent, hence quasi-coherent, cohomology and F is quasi-coherent, so Lf^*F and E\otimes^L_{O_X}Lf^*F lie in D_QCoh [lem-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-qcoh]. As f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the projection formula [lem-pc-projection-formula] identifies Rf_*E\otimes^L_{O_S}F with Rf_*(E\otimes^L_{O_X}Lf^*F). The complex inside Rf_* has cohomology in [a,b] by Step 2; its shift by b has no cohomology in positive degrees, so [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-uniform-truncation-bound] gives vanishing in degrees >= b+N. Since Rf_* is the total right derived functor [def-pc-derived-direct-image], computed on a K-injective complex that may be taken zero in degrees < a, there is no cohomology below a. Thus H^i(Rf_*E\otimes^L_{O_S}F)=0 for i\notin[a,b+N-1] and every quasi-coherent F.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.27.1 (Tag 08EV), projection-formula computation (Tag 08EU) and the final Tor-amplitude bound

proof.text: S is Noetherian, hence quasi-separated, and Rf_*E has coherent cohomology by [lem-pc-direct-image-bounded-coherent], so it lies in D_QCoh(O_S). By [lem-pc-tor-amplitude-qcoh-test] the vanishing of Step 3 for all quasi-coherent F gives H^i(Rf_*E\otimes^L_{O_S}F)=0 for i\notin[a,b+N-1] and every O_S-module F, which is the asserted finite Tor dimension.
